title: Surge smoothing & hybrid prefetch coordinator for console ingest
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: high-frequency tenants (microbursts) cause frequent head-of-line blocking in the console metrics real-time pipeline. Existing admission controllers either shed whole tenants or apply coarse throttles that harm high-priority customers and increase unit cost when cold-cache misses spike.

Proposal: implement a Surge Smoothing & Hybrid Prefetch Coordinator as a stream-side processor that sits just upstream of the per-shard admission queue. Key responsibilities: smoothing microbursts via a lightweight tenant reservoir, applying hybrid prefetch when KV/cache hints indicate hot prefixes, dynamically adjusting per-tenant admission windows based on tokenized cost and latency SLAs, and emitting rich signals for the Console Console-rt dashboards. The coordinator is designed to be shard-local to avoid global locks and to gracefully degrade to the existing admission controller when memory or CPU pressure is detected.

Core components: 1) Tenant microreservoir using a timing wheel + bounded priority queue to hold short-lived bursts for up to 500ms; 2) Prefetch predictor that samples recent request prefixes and issues KV cache pre-warms for predicted sequences; 3) Fairness allocator that prioritizes by customer tier and recent latency contribution; 4) Leak-based admission window that expands/contracts based on moving-average tail latency and token spend.

Expected benefits: reduce 99th percentile per-route latency by ~15-25% for bursty tenants, reduce unnecessary cold-cache CPU spikes via targeted prefetch, provide graceful tenant-level degradation instead of binary shedding, and lower tail-driven autoscaling churn.

comments: 2026-03-05 - Maya Chen: Created ticket. PoC prototype (rust) validated tenant reservoir semantics with synthetic hotkey trace. Observed 18% reduction in p99 on local bench for 95th-percentile burst traces.

2026-03-06 - Arjun Patel: Reviewed PoC. Notes: avoid global atomic counters across shards; prefer epoched lease tokens per shard. Action: integrate shard-epoch token approach and share code with ENG-950401 where prescaling logic lives.

2026-03-08 - Priya Rao (SRE): Added runbook request. We need a fallback path that emits a single Kafka event when the coordinator sheds to allow downstream billing and alerting to reconcile dropped events. SRE flagged retention for the shed-event topic to 7 days.

2026-03-09 - Design review (Amir Hassan): UX for observability: add 'smoothing_time_ms' and 'prefetch_score' to telemetry so Console can display tenant-level impact. Also suggest a 'heatmap' view for prefetch efficacy.

2026-03-10 - Arjun Patel: Implementation update: core coordinator implemented in the shard runner, integrated into the ingress path behind feature flag 'ingest.surge_smoothing_v1'. Added unit tests for timing wheel eviction and a microbenchmark harness. Initial perf run in qemu showed 12% CPU delta at peak under cfg A (reservoir=256, prefetch=false).

2026-03-11 - QA (Lina Ortiz): Integration tests failing intermittently in CI: observed rare stalls when combined with per-tenant backpressure + eviction. Mitigation: add a max-spin backoff and ensure eviction notifications are delivered to upstream admission controller. Filed follow-up ENG-424243 to harden eviction notifications.

2026-03-12 - Arjun Patel: Benchmarks after fixes: p99 improvement 20% on production trace replay; median latency unchanged. Preparing canary rollout plan and runbook. Documentation PR opened linked in implementation PR. Requesting review from Runtime and Platform teams.
